strengths: The paper considers an interesting and relevant application domain, i.e. the domain of predicting electron density in the ionosphere.
The notion of TEC and ionospheric modeling is interesting.
Proper language and structure of the paper
The paper describes a novel application of an autoencoder. The problem is uncommon and results of some reasonable quality were achieved.
weaknesses: The claim of introducing a new class of ‘oddly-shaped data' seems fuzzy and unwarranted; the TEC data presented appears to be simply a sequence of images with missing values, akin to some inpainting tasks or inputs for masked autoencoders.

Turning the data into sequences and applying models designed for natural language processing is invalid because there is no true order among the set of pixels; converting to a 1D sequence is arbitrary and may prevent transformers from learning meaningful co-occurrences, whereas image-based approaches would be more appropriate.

The presentation of prior/related work is misleading; the authors dismiss relevant image-based approaches (e.g., TEC Map Completion Through a Deep Learning Model: SNP-GAN, and VISTA) and unfairly claim modern GAN and other image ML techniques bias the result more than the proposed method, without comparing GAN latent codes to the proposed embeddings.
It is unclear if the presented results indicate substantial improvement; the reported increases in $R^2$ and MAE reductions are small and may not be statistically significant.

The motivation is unclear, particularly the notion of “oddly shaped data” and the contribution is unclear; the description suggests data is being gridded across the earth and the main problem appears to be sparse sampling.
There is no clear mathematical description of the data or method used, other than a block diagram in Figure 2 which appears to be mostly common components.
No methodological innovation; applying an existing approach to a new dataset does not meet the bar for methodological contributions.
Hints of controlling for confounding factors that would bias the representation and downstream prediction are not thoroughly explored; further investigation is recommended.
Insufficient literature review with many ML–ionospheric physics papers missing.
The method is not clearly described, making it unlikely that a reader can reproduce the work from the available material.
There is no comparison with another work.
Since the application is novel, it would be appropriate to describe the problem better.
Variable names are introduced but they are not explained in the text, e.g., Kp index, ap index etc.
